descriptions.title: Sibling of Maia — one engine, two products
descriptions.body: Naya does not reimplement chat, context, or language handling. naya_db.py imports Maia's maia_db, overwrites its DB_FILE to C:\NAYA\naya.db, and re-exports every symbol — so maia_context.build_context() and maia_lang.detect_input_language() run unchanged but against Naya's own data. naya_db MUST be imported before any maia_* module so the patch lands first. The result: Maia's battle-tested classroom engine becomes a single-owner personal assistant just by swapping the database and the persona. Maia and Naya stay separate projects; Maia may call Naya's API, but Naya never merges into Maia's codebase.

descriptions.title: Two databases, two jobs
descriptions.body: naya.db is the control plane — it inherits Maia's schema (config, llm_chain, conversations, the unused school tables) and is small (~900 KB). naya_brain.db is the file-intelligence store and is large (~2.3 GB): naya_scans (178 runs), naya_similarity_groups (~2.7M duplicate/fuzzy rows), naya_folder_insights, naya_intents, naya_operations, naya_drives, naya_settings. Keeping them apart means a giant scan history never bloats the conversational DB, and the brain store can be VACUUMed or pruned independently. The advisor, memory, scanner and executor all share naya_brain.db; FileHQ keeps its own filehq.db that Naya reads read-only.

descriptions.title: The 8-model failover chain (local-first)
descriptions.body: Naya's chain lives in the llm_chain table, ordered by priority, and _llm_call() walks it until one model returns usable text. The order is local-first and free-first: DeepSeek-R1 8B (primary, local), Cloudflare Qwen1.5 7B, GPT-OSS 20B (local), Gemma3:27b (local), Qwen3:4b (local), MiniMax M2.5 (OpenRouter free), GPT-OSS 120B (OpenRouter free), and Claude Sonnet as the paid last resort. Per-provider branches handle the Anthropic SDK, Ollama's OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions, and OpenRouter/Cloudflare. force_fast reorders to small local models for cheap intent extraction; force_sonnet promotes Claude for complex questions when personal.anthropic_mode=fallback. Nothing is hardcoded — reorder or disable a model by editing one DB row.

descriptions.title: LLM-first intent routing
descriptions.body: Rather than regex-matching commands, Naya sends every message to the LLM with a strict schema prompt (naya_llm_intent) and parses a JSON intent: {action, target, destination, format, schedule_time, chain_action, confidence}. naya_action_router.dispatch() maps the action to a permission-gated handler; if the model emits two actions in one message it fills chain_action and both run. The old keyword router (naya_intent_router) survives only as a fallback for when the LLM is unreachable, so file commands keep working offline. The same handler set serves chat, Telegram, and the Gradio File Manager via dispatch_action().

descriptions.title: Safety is structural
descriptions.body: Because Naya can touch the filesystem, every destructive path is gated. _is_approved() reads boolean flags from naya.db (file_scan_approved=true, file_modify_approved=false by default); a denied action returns the exact phrase to enable it. Deletes go to the recycle bin via send2trash unless permanent deletion is explicitly approved. The executor moves files to a NAYA_TRASH folder and logs each batch so undo_last() can restore them, and it never removes the keep copy (is_oldest) of a duplicate group. Folder access exceptions are tracked per-path in naya_folder_access.

descriptions.title: LAN-only, paused-but-running
descriptions.body: The QI registry marks Naya status 'paused' — no active feature development — yet QI_NayaBot and QI_NayaGradio are live NSSM services, so Naya still answers daily on Telegram and the local console. By deliberate design Naya is never exposed to the internet: Telegram uses outbound long-polling (no inbound port), and the only public surface is QI_NayaTunnel, a Cloudflare tunnel that exposes the read-mostly Gradio UI for occasional remote demos. The registry's standing instruction is explicit: never expose Naya's API via Cloudflare.
